newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain and Ukraine sign cooperation accords.
newsitem.headline: Spain and Ukraine sign cooperation accords.

text.p: Spain and Ukraine signed a wide-ranging set of bilateral agreements on Monday to coincide with the first day of a state visit by Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma.

Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes announced that he and his Ukrainian counterpart Hennady Udovenko signed accords on cultural and educational cooperation, social security, industrial and economic cooperation and air transport.
They also agreed to cooperate on defence matters.
Udovenko said Ukraine's principal foreign policy goal was to become a member of European structures and eventually of the European Union.
The EU recently signed a deal to give Ukraine about $675 million in technical aid.
The 15-member Union holds Ukraine in high regard for its efforts in introducing democracy since the break-up of the Soviet Union but says it must speed up moves towards micro-economic change.
At the start of his state visit, Kuchma met King Juan Carlos and Queen Sofia at Madrid's royal palace, where he was due to attend a gala dinner in his honour on Monday night.
